API `registerCallHierarchyProvider` does not work as expected and flakily
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed repro and for sticking with this. The flakiness came from the language-feature registry: when your provider and the built-in TypeScript provider scored the same for a file, the tie was broken by registration time, so whichever extension happened to register last won — hence the roughly 50/50 behavior. That tiebreak changed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/edf0b737f34d5050cc04bba08af7a1c509f87678: providers from built-in extensions are now de-prioritized when scores are equal, so a provider from an installed (non-built-in) extension wins consistently. No `extensionDependencies` workaround is needed anymore. Closing as resolved — please open a new issue if you still see a built-in provider taking over on a current build. The fix shipped in 1.78.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The flaky choice fits a tie between equal-score providers, broken by registration time, as extension activation races the built-in TypeScript provider. The diff passes isBuiltin through registerCallHierarchyProvider and ranks built-in providers below extension providers on a tie.

Keeping this discussion open to distinguish clearer regex guidance from a change to word-character semantics.

rows.title: VSCode Remote Compatibility Issue with Older GLIBC 2.17
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the context. A Node version does not uniquely determine its GLIBC requirement: that also depends on how the binary was built. The 1.98.2 server build distinguishes standard nodejs.org downloads from product-specific artifacts and includes a GLIBC 2.17 legacy packaging path: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1.98.2/build/gulpfile.reh.js. This explains why the official legacy server can behave differently from your OSS package without using the newer custom-sysroot workaround.

For your OSS build, a GLIBC 2.17-compatible Node binary alone is not sufficient unless the server's native dependencies are compatible too. Current official servers require GLIBC 2.28; the documented alternative for older hosts is the custom-sysroot workaround at https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/faq#_can-i-run-vs-code-server-on-older-linux-distributions, which is not an officially supported configuration. Closing this as a compatibility/build question rather than a VS Code bug.

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed troubleshooting write-up and the verbose logs — that rules out most of the usual causes.

On Windows this notification is shown when Electron's `safeStorage` reports that encryption is unavailable; the backend there is Windows DPAPI (see `EncryptionMainService` in `src/vs/platform/encryption/electron-main/encryptionMainService.ts`), which is also why `--password-store=wincred` has no effect — that switch only selects a Linux backend. Keeping this open: we'd like to pin down why DPAPI is failing on these machines, and the Linux-only fallback story means there's currently no supported alternative on Windows beyond running with `--use-inmemory-secretstorage` (secrets are then lost on restart). The Linux variant is tracked separately in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/187338.

rows.title: Deleted files in VS Code are being moved to Snap trash, consuming excessive disk space
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9dadd5ad1defcc3140bcdff44517284aeaf5bb91 by removing the Snap launcher's `XDG_DATA_HOME` override, so new Explorer deletions are no longer redirected to the Snap-specific trash directory. rows.verifyEvidence: The snap launcher no longer exports XDG_DATA_HOME as $SNAP_USER_DATA/.local/share, which had sent deleted files to a hidden trash inside the snap. Deletes now use the normal user trash, and the commit message names this trash problem.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/4e611a445d910b3a9e8be90f48c099e459613811 makes ChildProcessMonitor cancel its pending input and output refresh timers when disposed, so those callbacks no longer retain completed monitors until their deadlines. rows.verifyEvidence: The commit only cancels ChildProcessMonitor's pending debounce/throttle timers on dispose. That retention lasted only seconds. It leaves the debounce decorator unchanged and does not explain the reported persistent per-run leak. The message also says only 'Related to'.

rows.verifyEvidence: Commit deletes the deprecated `registerChatModelChangeListeners` from IChatService/ChatService and replaces it with per-controller listeners on `onDidCreateModel`/`chatModels`, so model changes now come from the chat model service. Unscoped 'code polish' is follow-up.

"workbench.colorCustomizations": {

rows.title: Git - on displaying .patch files, for --word-diff format text is NOT colored as for typical format
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The built-in Diff grammar highlights line-based additions and deletions, but does not currently recognize the inline [-OLD-] and {+NEW+} markers produced by Git's word-diff format. That grammar is maintained in https://github.com/textmate/diff.tmbundle; this remains open for an upstream grammar improvement followed by an update to VS Code's bundled grammar.

rows.title: Git - detecting filepath+line link in console diff not working for all formats
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and the additional context. The terminal’s Git diff detector currently requires the destination range to include a comma and count, so valid headers such as `@@ -7 +5 @@` are missed. That second number is a line count rather than a column.

The detector also recognizes only a hunk header at the beginning of a logical line, which explains the missing links for later space-separated headers in your compressed output. These belong with terminal link detection. Scrolling may be a separate case: the detector searches retained terminal buffer content for the file header, not only the visible viewport.

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. The startup error is `listen ENOTSUP` when creating the main IPC socket in `code-portable-data/user-data`; the file-watcher warning is separate and does not cause this exit.

VS Code's desktop user-data directory needs a filesystem that supports Unix sockets, as explained in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/137602#issuecomment-975501718. Use a socket-capable filesystem for the portable data, or disable portable mode so user data stays locally while the application remains on the external drive. In portable mode, `--user-data-dir` does not override the portable data location.

rows.title: The function of adding change summaries and reviews can be included in the git panel.
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the request. Copilot already provides this workflow in Source Control:

- Generate Commit Message (`github.copilot.git.generateCommitMessage`) fills the commit input with a generated summary.
- Code Review (`github.copilot.chat.review.changes`) reviews uncommitted changes; staged and unstaged review actions are also available. Review visibility depends on Copilot review availability and `github.copilot.chat.reviewAgent.enabled`.
- Review comments support applying suggested edits or continuing in inline chat (`github.copilot.chat.review.continueInInlineChat`), which automatically sends the finding as a fix prompt.

These existing actions cover the requested summary, review, and quick-fix workflow, so no additional buttons are needed.

chat.hookFilesLocations: rejects UNC/absolute paths inconsistently vs chat.pluginLocations + hooks inside agent plugins should be auto-discovered
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for clarifying. The restriction in `chat.hookFilesLocations` is intentional: it accepts workspace-relative or `~/` paths so the configuration remains portable across machines and remote environments. `chat.pluginLocations` has a different, machine-scoped path contract.

Hooks from plugins registered in `chat.pluginLocations` are already discovered without an additional `chat.hookFilesLocations` entry. The default location depends on the plugin format: `hooks.json` for Copilot format, `hooks/hooks.json` for Claude/OpenPlugin format, or `com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json` for AgentPlugin format; a manifest can also declare a custom hook path. If a plugin using its supported location is not discovered, please provide its manifest, hook JSON and directory layout so that specific failure can be investigated.

File links in terminal behave incorrectly when the file contains unicode characters
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Terminal file links use the editor's UTF-16 column numbering, rather than a count of displayed characters. In `#hello👋`, the emoji occupies two UTF-16 code units: column 7 is before it, column 8 falls inside it, and column 9 is after it. The editor intentionally moves a position inside a surrogate pair before the character, so `file.py:2:9` will navigate to the position you expected. Replacing the emoji with an ASCII character makes column 8 the end of the line, which explains the difference.

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed context. The built-in Plan definition is generated by Copilot and cached under extension global storage, so its `vscode-userdata` URI is an implementation detail rather than a supported agent-inheritance mechanism; there is no `.agent.md` instruction or frontmatter field that extends another agent. Shared behavior should instead live in your custom agent, an instruction file, or a reusable skill, or Plan should be invoked as a subagent.

Extensions using the proposed chat prompt-files API can call `vscode.chat.getCustomAgents(...)` and inspect the returned agent URIs, but a custom agent definition itself cannot invoke that extension API. Since the remaining request is a usage/API question rather than a reproducible VS Code defect, this can be closed as a question.

which extension in default vscode shipping turns autocomplete on?
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the question. The autocomplete popup is controlled by VS Code's editor, not by a single extension: `editor.quickSuggestions` controls suggestions while typing, and `editor.suggestOnTriggerCharacters` controls suggestions after characters such as `.`. The suggestions themselves can come from built-in language support or installed extensions; Copilot is not required for the popup.

To disable automatic popups, set `editor.quickSuggestions` and `editor.suggestOnTriggerCharacters` to `false`. If you mean inline ghost text instead, that is controlled separately by `editor.inlineSuggest.enabled`.

Multiline line commit messages
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. Git treats everything before the first blank line as the commit title. GitHub Desktop adds that blank line between its summary and description fields; VS Code's commit input accepts the complete message as entered.

For the same title and description in both applications, enter this in VS Code:

```text
Main line

Sub line.
```

Without the blank line, both lines belong to the title, which explains the combined summary in Desktop. This follows Git's documented message format: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#_discussion.

rows.title: Why does MCP require npx on the host; shouldn't it run in the devcontainer?

Keeping this open as a request to support an explicit remote execution choice for plugin-provided servers; configuring the server separately is an interim workaround.

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. `GIT_EDITOR` is a shell command, not a raw path: Git explicitly supports quoted executable paths and additional arguments (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-var). VS Code quotes the script path so locations containing spaces work correctly.

Passing the entire command to `cygpath` or `wslpath` treats those quotes as filename characters; path conversion needs to operate on the executable path rather than the complete editor command. If you prefer to configure your own editor command, disable `git.terminalGitEditor` and restart the terminal. The quoting itself is working as designed.

Thanks for the report. The active indent guide highlights a scope rather than always matching the selected line's indentation. rows.title: I cannot not see worktree function
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the question. Git worktrees themselves do not require a Copilot subscription: with a Git repository open, run **Git: Create Worktree** (`git.createWorktree`) from the Command Palette.

The **Workspace / Worktree** picker in Copilot CLI sessions controls isolation for that session type; it is separate from the built-in Git commands and is not an option shared by every chat mode. rows.title: Fuzzy search pattern doesn't match words if it's corresponding parts start not after a delimiter/from a capital letter
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. IntelliSense requires the first matching character to be at a word start by default, so `fetch` matches `git.autoFetch` but not `git.autofetch`. Set `"editor.suggest.matchOnWordStartOnly": false` to include matches inside lowercase words.

The scorer supports this through `firstMatchCanBeWeak: true`; the supplied assertion uses the default options, which intentionally reject that match.

rows.title: Webview resources fail silently with ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES when a webview loads thousands of files (Linux renderer keeps default 1024 nofile soft limit)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the independent confirmation. This resource-exhaustion case was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/17d3b86b9361cba49d8d0238787d9aa590e657ca: desktop webviews now queue host-backed resource transfers and limit them to 32 active response bodies, including their cache writes, rather than starting the entire burst at once. This implements the throttling alternative described here without requiring a higher renderer file-descriptor limit, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.130.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: On Electron, the service worker now allows at most 32 host-backed resource bodies at once and holds each slot for the stream's lifetime. This is the reporter's suggested throttle, and it bounds renderer FD use under the 1024 soft limit. Leftover: failures are still not shown to users.

rows.title: Worktrees omit gitignored .claude folder, preventing CLAUDE settings/plugins from roaming
rows.proposedComment:

VS Code currently supports copying an ignored `.claude` folder with `"git.worktreeIncludeFiles": [".claude/**"]`, or sharing it with `"git.worktreeSymlinkFolders": [".claude"]`; edits through the symlink also affect the source checkout. These settings apply when VS Code creates the worktree, not when you run `git worktree add` directly.

The general behavior is documented at https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/sourcecontrol/branches-worktrees#_include-files-when-creating-a-worktree. rows.title: Cursor doesn't follow page when scrolling with Ctrl+Arrow keys in VS Code
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and the update confirmation. Ctrl+Up/Down is intentionally bound to `scrollLineUp` and `scrollLineDown`, which scroll the editor without moving the caret. The same Visual Studio-style request was previously addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/111734#issuecomment-737212368.

For caret-following scrolling, the built-in `editorScroll` command supports `revealCursor: true`, with `to: "up"` or `"down"` and `by: "line"`. This keeps the caret inside the viewport when it would otherwise scroll out of view. I understand that you are asking to change the defaults rather than customize your bindings; the existing defaults deliberately preserve the caret position, so this is being closed as designed.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed repro and for confirming it again on 1.137.0. Tracing the code, these look like two distinct gaps: the Edit > Find/Replace menu items are bound to the generic `actions.find`/`actions.replace` commands, which only operate on a Monaco code editor (src/vs/editor/contrib/find/browser/findController.ts) and simply no-op when a webview (like the Markdown preview) is active — there's no fallback to the webview's own find command (`editor.action.webvieweditor.showFind` in webviewCommands.ts). Separately, the webview's find-related context keys are scoped to its own DOM container (overlayWebview.ts), so Ctrl+F's keybinding only resolves once that container actually gets DOM focus, matching the extra-click behavior you saw. Routing this to the webview/markdown owners for a look, since it likely needs a menu-command fallback plus a focus-on-show tweak rather than a one-line fix.

Thanks for the report and the keybindings file. Your Ctrl+Right binding uses `cursorWordStartRight`, but Ctrl+Left still uses the default `cursorWordLeft`, which intentionally skips some single-character separators. To use matching word-start navigation, bind Ctrl+Left to `cursorWordStartLeft` and Ctrl+Shift+Left to `cursorWordStartLeftSelect`, using the same `when` condition as your right-arrow bindings.

These commands navigate editor-defined word and separator starts; they are not defined as stopping at every regex `\b` match, including word ends before whitespace. The difference shown by these bindings is expected behavior.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the very thorough writeup — this is a serious one. I traced the persistence path: `storeSessions()` in `chatServiceImpl.ts` is only invoked from `saveState()`, which itself only runs on the storage service's periodic/shutdown `onWillSaveState` event (or an explicit rename via `setChatSessionTitle`). There's no per-turn trigger to persist ops as they happen, and any write failure in `writeSession()` is swallowed into telemetry with no user-visible signal — which lines up with the stub `kind:0`-only files and silent disappearance you found. This looks closely related to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337278 filed today against the same subsystem. Routing to the chat area for further investigation into why the periodic save can be skipped for a session's whole lifetime (remote connectivity is a reasonable working theory) and whether persistence should be made more resilient (surfaced errors, more frequent/triggered saves, or reconciling `isEmpty` against the actual file).

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. Regex search follows JavaScript semantics: `\b` uses the regex definition of a word character, which does not include `ä`, even in Unicode mode. Consequently, `\bB\b` matches the `B` in `Bänder` as designed.

To select standalone `B` in the editor, turn off regex search, enter `B`, and enable **Match Whole Word** (`toggleFindWholeWord`). This uses `editor.wordSeparators` and excludes `Bänder` with the default settings.

rows.title: Claude Agent unavailable with Claude3PIntegration=true: unchecked, locked setting displays “Enabled by organization”
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and logs. This looks like intended behavior rather than a bug: `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled` is governed by the `Claude3PIntegration` policy, whose value callback (`thirdPartyAgentEnabledValue` in `src/vs/platform/policy/common/copilotManagedSettings.ts`) deliberately forces the setting to `false` whenever the account is governed by Copilot managed settings — on purpose, so a managed-settings-governed account can't bypass enterprise controls through a device-level MDM policy or a user setting. For an enterprise-managed GitHub account with a Copilot Enterprise seat, that's very likely why your `Claude3PIntegration=true` MDM policy and your explicit user setting are both overridden. The 'overlapping keys' log line is expected in this situation — it's the device policy and the managed-settings-derived policy both resolving the same key, with the managed-settings value taking precedence. I'd agree the generic 'Managed by organization' indicator doesn't make clear *which direction* a policy is enforcing, which is worth a UX follow-up, but the underlying lock itself matches the documented design. If you believe your organization's managed settings shouldn't be suppressing Claude for your account, that's a question for your GitHub Copilot enterprise administrator rather than a VS Code defect.

rows.title: Up arrow in python debug console does not work as expected after using "Evaluate in Debug Console"

This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d9d04e97b7079bfb40b5c2662379e0c55230fca7 and shipped in VS Code 1.91.0 — expressions sent via "Evaluate in Debug Console" are now added to the REPL input history, so up-arrow retrieves them as expected. Closing as completed. Please open a new issue if you still see a problem on the latest build.

rows.title: Detached DOM nodes memory leak
Unable to drag views to reorder or move to different pane
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for confirming this directly in vscode.dev. The same iPadOS drag-and-drop gap is already tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/86457, including activity-bar and panel movement with an attached mouse or trackpad. This report adds useful confirmation from iPadOS 15.4 with both a Magic Keyboard trackpad and a Logitech mouse.

/duplicate of #86457
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report that views/panes cannot be dragged in VS Code's web UI under iPadOS Safari, the same missing touch drag-and-drop support for moving views.

rows.title: cmd+click behavior for Goto Definition and a Document Link
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report. This is the same simultaneous link-opening and definition-navigation problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/81520, including its example of documentation links and source definitions on the same Go import.

The Terraform example and Ruby-LSP/Sorbet interaction here provide additional cases for that work. The attempted fix was reverted in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/169667 after breaking Markdown links when a definition provider returned no result; that regression also needs to be accounted for when resolving the canonical issue.

/duplicate of #81520
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report the same core defect. When a text range has both a document link and a definition, ctrl/cmd+click runs both, so the link opens and Go to Definition also navigates; neither takes precedence.

rows.title: Bad behaviour for named pipe (mkfifo)
Prevent menu selection from static mouse hover
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The current quick-fix widget now preserves keyboard selection when it opens beneath a stationary pointer, fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/68be8adf6e379475b6466ad050236ff6546a555d. The linked custom-menu fix also landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329507, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.138.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both diffs stop a menu opening under a stationary pointer from stealing focus via mouseover — the action widget ignores initial hover until real pointer movement, matching the quick-fix item re-selection reported.

rows.title: View multiple debug consoles side by side in editor areas
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the request — being able to cross-reference debug consoles side by side is a real workflow need. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/201772, which tracks making the debug console openable as an editor (enabling side-by-side layout, floating windows, etc.) — consolidating the discussion there.

/duplicate of #201772

rows.title: File nesting `expand: false` setting not respected in folders with a single child file nest
Git - Prune On Fetch
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. Local branches remaining after fetch pruning is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/183906. The existing `git.pruneOnFetch` setting prunes stale remote-tracking refs, but does not delete local branches. This report adds the Azure DevOps auto-complete workflow on Windows and a claimed change between VS Code 1.66 and 1.67; those details remain relevant to the cleanup discussion.

/duplicate of #183906
rows.verifyEvidence: Both ask for local branches to be removed automatically once their remote branch is deleted and pruned. A calls this a 1.66 regression, but git prune only removes remote-tracking refs, so A needs the feature B requests.

rows.title: Unify inline edit experience
When Debug: Inline Values is set together with Word wrap, breakpoints are not correctly focused
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and detailed reproduction. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9aaf087e6bb1fff5d032e3885d577db289f0f24b and shipped in VS Code 1.90.0; wrapped debug inline values now preserve the cursor's vertical position in the viewport.
rows.verifyEvidence: Diff explicitly compensates scroll when inline-value decorations reflow wrapped lines, preserving the cursor's viewport position — exactly the reported mechanism where values applied after focusing push the paused line away.

rows.title: [CustomTextEditor extensions] Untitled document content is lost when doing "Reopen with..." custom text editor
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/131fadee2b35ad00e7ec2347598a75e6211861c5 and shipped in VS Code 1.121.0 — the untitled document data is now correctly passed to the custom editor extension before the untitled text model is reverted, so content is preserved when using "Reopen with…" on an untitled file. Please open a new issue if you still see this on the latest build.
rows.verifyEvidence: Diff removes the eager untitledTextModel.revert() in CustomEditorInput that emptied the untitled model on reopen-with, deferring it until after untitledDocumentData is delivered — exactly the mechanism producing the reported document length 0.

rows.title: Add context menu contribution point to Watch Variables Pane
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the feature request! The `debug/watch/context` menu contribution point was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/a16e9fc056b2e7c98e843eefefc2075169ae593d and shipped in VS Code 1.103. Extensions can now contribute context menu items to the Watch pane by targeting the `debug/watch/context` menu in their `package.json`. I believe this covers the request — please open a new issue if you still see a gap.

rows.title: Allow extensions to contribute Group Policy
Expose access token expiration time from `AuthenticationSession`
Renaming a folder that is locked by an application locks up explorer for ~1 minute and eventually fails with EPERM
Conflicting File Nesting Patterns
Allow (modifier)+click for "step in target"
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the request. This exact modifier-click interaction is already part of the open Smart Step Into proposal at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/123879, including selecting a displayed step target directly from the paused source editor, so consolidating the work there.

/duplicate of #123879
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request the same capability: selecting a step-into target via modifier+click, which B explicitly proposes as its 'Modifier Key + Inline Decorators' solution for smart step into.

rows.title: Make terminal bright colors lighter than regular colors in Light+
Add a setting to let CJK font width == 2 * ASCII font width
[html] Duplicate double quotes are inserted for HTML attributes when working over SSH
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The underlying stale-edit race was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/1846f69774571e62bf81c16b2496ae739978277b: snippet insertion now checks the renderer model version and declines delayed HTML quote insertion after newer typing, including the higher-latency Remote SSH case described here. The fix shipped in 1.75.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The commit makes the main thread reject insertSnippet when the model version is stale, which could fix late quote insertion over SSH. But it targets Emmet, and the diff does not show the HTML auto-insert path calling it.

rows.title: Extension API around quick picks/input boxes is inconsistent
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for filing this and for the PR work on https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/157022. The gap was closed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3bd2b70f4a40203cbb01a0cecd72343b65c00108 — `InputBox.valueSelection` (and `QuickPick.valueSelection`) shipped on the stable API in VS Code 1.73.0. Closing as completed.

rows.title: SCM file decorations are misaligned or different sizes
Cursor no longer selects entire tab (accessibility issue)
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for raising this — I appreciate the accessibility perspective. The block cursor width on tabs was intentionally changed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/a449148a14d to fix https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/151959, and the current 1-character-width rendering matches other editors like SublimeText.

As discussed in the thread, the recommended path for restoring the old full-tab-width behavior is an extension using editor decorations. Closing as by-design, but please open a new issue if you'd like to request a built-in setting for this — that would be a feature request the team could evaluate.

rows.title: Handle rate limits on docker.io
`Auto Save` menu state not updated properly (vscode-web)
Broken copy/paste menu in extension description
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was the same webview focus defect tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/141080. It was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d4b4c327798c27807c2710fa15a420c5dd17429d and shipped in VS Code 1.88.0, so context-menu Copy now reaches the active webview.
rows.verifyEvidence: Extension details render in a webview; the diff keeps the webview treated as focused while its context menu is open, fixing exactly the reported case where menu Copy failed but Ctrl+C worked.

rows.title: Don't use actions-anti-pattern for filter box rendering
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for filing and driving this cleanup, Johannes. All six tracked items appear to be resolved:

- **Filter boxes** → adopted `FilterViewPane` (PR https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/163132) for REPL, markers, and comments
- **Output selector** → converted to submenu pattern (PR https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/162966)
- **Testing filter** → dead code removed (PR https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/163574)
- **Terminal** → unused action removed; `SwitchTerminal` kept as a real action (PR https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/178420)

The unchecked `repl.ts` item already extends `FilterViewPane`, and its `SelectRepl` action is a real functional command (switches debug sessions), matching the same conclusion reached for the terminal's `SwitchTerminal`. I believe this can be closed as completed.

rows.title: The representation of a variable introspected in the Debug Console can be clipped on VSCode.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report. The original missing final line with `debug.console.wordWrap` disabled was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/162101 in commit https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7b7f5a046646993c2b6ee00b76d4eef75a012341 and shipped in VS Code 1.72.0; the corrected evaluation-result sizing remains on current main. The later discussion reproduced differing vertical spacing but not the original clipping, so this can be closed as completed.
rows.verifyEvidence: Report shows multiline variable output clipped in the Debug Console; the commit fixes the REPL viewer's row-count/height estimation for multiline evaluation results, the exact mechanism that truncated such rendered values.

rows.title: [less] support `each` in keyframes
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and the updated-version confirmation. This is the same LESS parser issue tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/149193, including the false diagnostics for `each` inside `@keyframes`, so the discussion can be consolidated there.

/duplicate of #149193
rows.verifyEvidence: Both issues report the same bug: the LESS parser flags valid `each(...)` mixin calls inside `@keyframes` as syntax errors ("{ expected"). It is the same false-positive diagnostic in the same at-rule context.

rows.title: Markdown preview does not scroll to top on new URI
Possible issue with configured affinity on vscode.dev (info message)
[css] Add new CSS color functions
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request and contributions. This was implemented by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-css-languageservice/pull/306 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-css-languageservice/pull/436, then integrated into VS Code by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/91b02efb2350b7cc8ed28591f22f7c9e5445a892. It shipped in VS Code 1.117.0, and all four requested functions now provide color previews.
rows.verifyEvidence: Commit is an ESM/module-format migration of the HTML/CSS language servers; the bundled languageservice bump is incidental and the diff shows no lch/oklch/lab/oklab color-decorator support.

rows.title: [json] Support json-schema draft 2020-12
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and detailed context. JSON Schema draft 2020-12 support, including `$dynamicRef`/`$dynamicAnchor` and completion through dynamic references, was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-json-languageservice/commit/257468d7a005a9ed808aa7f0f587915fec9817d5 and integrated into VS Code by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/041d1b6643abf1aae6c94c0877cb4699a028ca0d, so this can be closed as completed.
rows.verifyEvidence: The draft 2020-12 meta-schema reaches nested subschemas through `$dynamicRef: "#meta"`, which was previously flagged as unsupported. The commit resolves `$dynamicRef`/`$dynamicAnchor`, including dynamic scope across documents, and tests completion through them.

rows.title: Change undo/redo to time based, AKA allow undo without erasing redo
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the suggestion. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/20889, which tracks undo branches — preserving redo history when new edits are made after undoing — with extensive community discussion and a prototype. Consolidating there.

/duplicate of #20889
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request non-destructive undo history that preserves alternate futures after undoing then editing, citing the same loss scenario; linear-rewind vs tree is a UI variant of one capability.

rows.title: Alt+Space behavior disruptive and inconsistent
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and video. The behavior you described — Alt+Space showing a VS Code custom menu instead of the native Windows system menu depending on mouse position — was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/af87ab952e96f3d47cde4b70159d10d5b146030d, which shipped in VS Code 1.101.0. On Windows, Alt+Space now always opens the native OS system menu regardless of cursor position. Please open a new issue if you still see unexpected behavior on the latest build.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff gates the cursor-x-dependent custom-menu branch to Linux, so on Windows Alt+Space always falls through to the OS system menu — exactly the mouse-position-dependent inconsistency the Windows reporter described.

rows.title: A full absolute path does not work
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/05e3b001da1 — `ResourceGlobMatcher` now detects absolute paths in configured expressions and matches against the full filesystem path when relative matching misses. Shipped in VS Code 1.79.0. Please open a new issue if you still see trouble with absolute paths in `explorer.autoRevealExclude` on the latest build.
rows.verifyEvidence: ResourceGlobMatcher.matches now detects absolute-path keys (hasAbsolutePath) and re-matches the resource's full fsPath, exactly the mechanism that made an absolute-path glob entry fail to match the reported file.

rows.title: "editor.inlineSuggest.enabled" add extra quote when using tab in a "workbench.colorCustomizations" settings
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the confirmations and updated context. This may have been fixed since the original report, but the latest reports do not yet establish whether the same issue remains on the current build. Could someone who still sees it test the latest VS Code version with extensions disabled and provide the exact settings, JSON content, cursor/Tab sequence, and a short recording? Issues with the `info-needed` label automatically close after 7 days without a reply.
rows.verifyEvidence: The report gives exact [jsonc] settings, a numbered quote/paste/Tab sequence and recordings. A maintainer reproduced the wrong replace range and traced it to suggestInlineCompletions.ts, so the current build can be checked directly.

rows.title: Remote SSH incorrectly strips empty but defined environment variables from shell environment
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and investigation. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b907d7875a8840b457447e5c6853345d7805493e: integrated terminal environment creation now preserves explicitly empty values such as `TESTVAR3=""`, including on the remote terminal path. Closing as completed. The fix shipped in 1.77.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff replaces a falsy check with an undefined/null check in mergeNonNullKeys, so empty-string variables are retained when building terminal env — exactly the defined-but-empty stripping the report describes, with a regression test.

rows.title: Right To Left text with numbers
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. RTL text rendering with mixed numbers/LTR content is tracked by the canonical issue https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/11770, which has been receiving active fixes recently (decoration-based RTL support, `dir="auto"` on RTL tokens). Consolidating the discussion there.

/duplicate of #11770
rows.verifyEvidence: A's mis-ordered digits in Hebrew text is a bidi-rendering defect that only full RTL/bidi support—the exact capability B tracks for Hebrew/Arabic source files—would deliver, so B's resolution necessarily covers A.

rows.title: Alt+NumPadKey with num lock will still write the alt code character on top of performing the action
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/22364, which tracks the same behavior where an Alt+numpad keybinding runs and Windows also inserts the corresponding Alt-code character; this report adds the Alt+Numpad4 navigation and JAWS context there.

/duplicate of #22364
rows.verifyEvidence: On Windows, both report that Alt plus a numpad arrow key with Num Lock off runs the VS Code keybinding and also types the Windows Alt-code character. A uses go back, B uses move line; the cause is the same.

rows.title: Extra inlay hints appearing in minimap
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report. A closely related bug (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/149572) was fixed in May 2022 — it addressed duplicate inlay hints in the minimap when toggling offUnlessPressed. Since this report came in after that fix, can you check whether the issue still reproduces on the latest VS Code build? If it does, sharing a minimal LSP server repro (or the server logs showing the duplicated hints) would help narrow this down.

Note: issues labeled `info-needed` will auto-close after 7 days without a reply.

rows.title: Cannot paste full file paths after copying file from file explorer on Linux
'Open recent' menu takes up full width of the window when it contains an entry with very long path
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d8dcf962241864c7a1631e3b8a8acb00e88a9d9d via https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329710: Open Recent labels are now middle-truncated to 120 characters, preventing very long paths from expanding the submenu across the window. The fix shipped in 1.133.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: Commit caps Open Recent entry labels at 120 chars via truncateMiddle in MenubarControl.getOpenRecentActions — the shared base path producing those entries — directly bounding the over-wide submenu caused by very long paths.

rows.title: Hidden panels create actions that are disposed of on startup
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed trace. This is the hidden-panel case of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/163234, which already tracks panel actions being created and immediately disposed on startup; the `refactorPreview` example here is useful evidence for that broader work.

/duplicate of #163234
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report the same startup defect from the same perf tracker: composite/panel actions are eagerly created during registration then immediately disposed when the composite isn't shown; B already proposes deferring creation until visible.

rows.title: Reset Menu doesn't show up when all items are visible, even if some are hidden by default
Problems pane gives incorrect advice about `launch.json`.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/32dee77a1a78b96719f4f12a1eee287b18827138 and shipped in VS Code 1.79.0 — the platform-specific override sections (`windows`, `osx`, `linux`) in `launch.json` now use a separate schema definition that correctly excludes `name`, `type`, and `request`. Please reopen if you still see this on a current build.

rows.title: [CustomTextEditor extensions] Editors of untitled files open twice when restarting.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This restoration path was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/614fb12a9394d55abfba75818fe8fdf5ca2d58d1: an untitled backup now recognizes the existing custom editor instead of opening a second text-editor tab, with regression coverage for that case. The fix shipped in 1.121.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The handler's isOpen now matches any editor sharing the untitled resource, so backup restore no longer creates a duplicate UntitledTextEditorInput beside the custom editor — exactly the double-open-on-restart reported.

rows.title: Disassembly view: context menus
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for requesting this — a disassembly view context menu was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/212500 and shipped in VS Code 1.100. It includes Copy Address, Toggle Breakpoint, and an extension contribution point (`DebugDisassemblyContext`) so debug adapters can add their own entries.

More advanced items like Run to Cursor and display-column toggles are tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/129762 (Disassembly View: Milestone 2). Closing this one as the core context-menu infrastructure is in place — please comment on #129762 for specific follow-ups.

rows.title: explorer.excludeGitIgnore is not working in a multiroot workspace when .gitignore is outside the workspace
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for reporting this. The root cause — the explorer's gitignore filter only reads `.gitignore` files it encounters inside the workspace folder tree, missing ancestor `.gitignore` files above the workspace root — is the same defect tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/189951, which has a simpler repro and carries `help wanted`. Consolidating the discussion there.

/duplicate of #189951
rows.verifyEvidence: Both stem from explorer.excludeGitIgnore scoping .gitignore resolution to the workspace folder instead of walking up to the git repo root, so ancestor .gitignore rules are never applied; fixing B covers A.

rows.title: Uncaught Error: Illegal value for lineNumber
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. The identical hover stack is now tracked with current cross-platform telemetry in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318008; this report's 2023 occurrence and matching Monaco consumer evidence remain useful historical context, so consolidating the investigation there.

/duplicate of #318008
rows.verifyEvidence: Same error signature: getLineMaxColumn throws 'Illegal value for lineNumber' from markdownHoverParticipant.computeSync in the hover operation's sync computation; frame differences only reflect later builds and refactoring.

rows.title: [a11y] Non-modal find / replace dialog should programmatically identify itself
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/56f11d9b49fbb60e4aa1e5546eca77ca5b504bbb: the editor find widget now identifies itself as a “Find / Replace” dialog, and its close button belongs directly to that dialog rather than the find-input group. These changes remain present on current main, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.80.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff gives the find widget root role='dialog' and a localized 'Find / Replace' aria-label. It also moves the close button out of find-part to sit directly in the dialog, which is exactly the pattern the report asked for.

rows.title: [Bug] VSCode.dev - Releasing the mouse outside of the editor area triggers a `click` event in Firefox
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. This is the same underlying issue as https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/199477, which tracks the Firefox-specific behavior where releasing the mouse outside the editor after starting a selection fires a spurious click. That issue has a maintainer response and an open fix PR (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/304955) — consolidating the discussion there.

/duplicate of #199477
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report the identical Firefox web/monaco defect: a mousedown-initiated editor text selection released over an outside button or link spuriously fires that element's click, same trigger chain and mechanism.

rows.title: Don't rely on QuickInputService in EditorResolverService
Rendered whitespace characters non-uniform
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and confirmations. The editor still uses SVG whitespace rendering by default, but the relevant renderer and Chromium stack have changed since this was reported; could you confirm whether this still occurs on the latest build with a negative `window.zoomLevel`, and include the Windows display scaling where it reproduces? As a workaround, `editor.experimentalWhitespaceRendering: "font"` or `"off"` avoids the issue. Issues labeled `info-needed` automatically close after 7 days without a reply.
rows.verifyEvidence: The thread already gives Windows 10, display scaling of 100% and 125%, the zoom levels that trigger it (-1, -3), and the cause (`editor.experimentalWhitespaceRendering` svg). The SVG renderer is still the default, so a maintainer can test it directly.

rows.title: file explorer flash when startup
v1.76 ZoneWidget right-click context is affected by sash and scrollbar
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The underlying context-menu stacking problem was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/70af9b11638cbb4e4b4ec997916510852cdd61c8: menus from fixed-overflow embedded editors are now mounted at the window root, so a ZoneWidget's sash and scrollbar no longer paint over them. The fix shipped in 1.135.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: Issue body is only two screenshots with no text, so the reported sash/scrollbar interaction cannot be matched against this commit's shadow-root mounting and z-index layering change.

rows.title: Activitybar input gets captured by file explorer
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and video. This issue has been waiting for confirmation for a while — could you check whether this still reproduces on the latest VS Code stable or insiders build on your Chromebook? A lot has changed in Electron and Chromium since early 2023, and this may have been resolved upstream.

If it does still reproduce, please share the new VS Code and Electron versions so we can investigate further. This issue will auto-close in 7 days without a reply.

rows.title: [PerfSampleError] `documentSymbolsTree`
Git - Problem with Placeholder in settings.json using git.path
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and detailed logs. Environment-variable resolution in `git.path` is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/116495. Your portable Windows setup adds useful evidence: `${env:GIT_CMD_PATH}` is tried literally, so an installed system Git wins; without that installation, discovery eventually finds portable Git through PATH. Consolidating this case there preserves that distinction.

/duplicate of #116495
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report that git.path does not substitute placeholder/environment variables: the git extension probes the literal unresolved string, then falls back to default install paths. In A, that fallback finds C:\Program Files\Git first.

rows.title: The material icons of folders in the HTML files are not displayed. Did anyone have such a problem?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you retest this on the latest VS Code and provide the active file icon theme, a minimal folder layout, and whether it also occurs with the built-in Seti icon theme? This issue will automatically close after 7 days without the requested information.
rows.verifyEvidence: The report says the Material icon theme is in use and gives the context: folder entries in HTML path completions show no icons until '//' is typed. A maintainer can reproduce that with html-language-features path completion and the suggest widget's folder icon rendering.

rows.title: [linked editing] Linked editing stops syncing on quick edits
Iframe content in WebviewPanel appears to drop Copy/Paste and other keyboard events, as well as context menu events
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and reproduction steps. This is tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/129178, which covers the same root cause — keyboard shortcuts and input events from iframes inside webviews are swallowed on macOS. The context menu part you noted is another symptom of the same event-forwarding gap. Consolidating the discussion there.

/duplicate of #129178
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report that a nested iframe inside a webview on macOS swallows keyboard shortcuts like Cmd+C while the Edit menu works, i.e. the same missing key-event forwarding from nested frames.

rows.title: `editor.action.moveLinesDownAction` doesn't work properly with vertical selection
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and the detailed analysis. This is the same consecutive-cursor line-movement problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/11809: only the primary cursor's line moves and secondary cursors are lost. The final-line cursor exception and your notes about same-line cursors and indentation are useful requirements to carry into that discussion and the existing fix proposal, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/68695.

/duplicate of #11809
rows.verifyEvidence: Both issues report the same defect: with multiple cursors, move line up/down discards every cursor except the primary and moves only that line. A uses vertical selection to create the cursors, which is the same mechanism.

rows.title: Allow display prop on markdown span style
Increase maximum problems per file (or allow customization)
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the request and community support. This is covered by the older open Backlog issue https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/172696, which tracks the identical request to increase or configure the 1,000-problem limit. Consolidating there keeps the implementation discussion in one place.

/duplicate of #172696
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request the identical capability — raise or make configurable the 1000 problems-per-file limit set in #49687 — with identical titles and the same prior request #159223 cited.

rows.title: Multiselect via ctrl+d case insensitivity makes it useless
While draging to create mutipile-cursors the start point is where the cursor used to be rather than the position where I clicked.
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and the comparison videos. The main issue — column selection anchoring from the cursor position rather than the click position — is already tracked at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/5402, which requests the same improvement. Consolidating the discussion there.

rows.title: cursorUp/down behavior inconsistent when moving from selection
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report. This is actually intentional behavior: when you press ↑ with a selection, the cursor collapses to the **start** of the selection; when you press ↓, it collapses to the **end**. This is the same pattern as ← (collapses to start) and → (collapses to end), providing a consistent mental model across all arrow keys.

This convention is common across text editors and platform text controls — the idea is that the direction of movement determines which end of the selection you land on, regardless of which end the caret was on. The behavior has been stable since 2016.

Closing as by-design, but feel free to reopen if you believe there's a case we've overlooked.

Unicode characters like ♣♠♥♦ may not have uniform monospace widths in all fonts — this is expected behavior from the font itself, not a rendering bug in VS Code.

Using a strict monospace font (Consolas, Inconsolata, JetBrains Mono, etc.) resolves this. Closing as by-design since VS Code correctly renders what the font provides.

rows.title: Can't launch additional windows via `code` from cli.
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed logs — they actually reveal the likely cause. In your log output, the second instance's args include:

```
extensionDevelopmentPath: [ '$HOME/.vscode-oss/extensions/undefined_publisher.wallbash-0.0.1' ]
```

This argument shouldn't be present when you just run `code --disable-extensions --verbose ./tmp2`. When it's present, VS Code routes the request through the extension development host path instead of opening a normal new window — which explains the observed behavior.

Could you check:
1. What does `which code` or `type code` return? Is it a wrapper script (common on Arch with Code-OSS packages)?
2. Does the issue persist if you launch directly via the binary (e.g. `/usr/lib/code-oss/code-oss ./tmp2`)?
3. Is there anything in your shell startup (`.zshrc`, etc.) that aliases or wraps the `code` command?

The `undefined_publisher.wallbash-0.0.1` extension path suggests something in your environment is injecting `--extensionDevelopmentPath` into the launch arguments.

Note: this issue will auto-close in 7 days without a reply.

rows.title: Activating display pointer trails makes text editing pointer disappear
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and for noting this affects other applications too. This is a known Windows 11 24H2 bug that affects cursor rendering in Chromium-based applications (including VS Code's Electron shell). It's been reported and confirmed across several issues here:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/236807
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/239422

**Workarounds:**
- Change the Windows cursor scheme (Settings → Accessibility → Mouse pointer and touch → change the pointer style)
- Increase pointer size to 2 or above
- Disable pointer trails

Since the root cause is in Windows / Chromium rather than VS Code, there isn't a fix we can apply on our side. The upstream bug is tracked in the Chromium project. Closing as not reproducible from VS Code's side — please open a new issue if you see this persist after a future Windows update addresses the underlying cursor compositing bug.

rows.title: "Hold Shift to drop into editor" not working in Wayland
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the thorough report and the excellent root-cause analysis in the comments. This is an upstream limitation: Chromium (and by extension Electron) does not populate modifier key state (`shiftKey`, `ctrlKey`, etc.) on `DragEvent` objects under Wayland. VS Code's `isDragIntoEditorEvent` in `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorDropTarget.ts` relies on `e.shiftKey`, so it silently fails.

The workaround attempts described in comment 6 (tracking keydown/keyup state, or using Electron IPC) are blocked because no keyboard events fire during drag-and-drop on Wayland.

This should be tracked as an `upstream` issue against Chromium/Electron. Labeling accordingly so it stays visible until upstream resolves modifier key reporting during drag events on Wayland.

This is now implemented by `chat.defaultModel`, and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/de7b8e2811af44a1f2683c21de870a5059536d5f completed the behavior by ensuring every new empty conversation applies that configured default instead of inheriting the previous session's model; explicit choices within an existing conversation remain preserved. The fix shipped in 1.131.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: Commit only makes an explicitly configured `chat.defaultModel` win on empty sessions and is inert when unset; the issue asks about ExP/CAPI-driven defaults overriding sticky last-used models.

rows.title: Raise or make configurable the hard 200-result cap in Copilot’s grep_search
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and the concrete repo evidence — this was really helpful. The grep_search result cap is now configurable as of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/33dec983b5b71623807b353abab2629cf25a76b3: you can set `github.copilot.chat.tools.grepSearch.maxResultsCap` to raise (or lower) the 200-result default, and `github.copilot.chat.tools.grepSearch.defaultMaxResults` to control the default when the LLM doesn't request a specific count. This should be available in the latest Insiders build. Please reopen if you still see issues on the latest version.

rows.title: Task commands retrieved from a command won't be recognized as absolute
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and workaround analysis. This is a known bug — the task system resolves `${command:…}` variables only after `_resolveAndFindExecutable` has already checked whether the command is an absolute path, so the unresolved variable string fails the check and gets the workspace folder prepended.

This is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/160891 (which also carries the `help wanted` label). Your cross-platform workaround detail (`\\?\` prefix on Windows) is useful context — consolidating there.

/duplicate of #160891
rows.verifyEvidence: Both: a 'process' task whose command is a ${command:…} variable is prepended with the workspace cwd because the unresolved variable string isn't detected as an absolute path; shell tasks unaffected.

rows.title: Selected model keeps switching back to GPT 4.1 / Sonnet 4
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was caused by the `chat.defaultLanguageModel` A/B experiment, which was overriding persisted model selections when new chat sessions started — it was removed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b409152750e and shipped in 1.106.0. The model selection logic has since been significantly refactored and hardened. Please open a new issue if you still see unexpected model switching on the latest build.
rows.verifyEvidence: The commit deletes the chat.defaultLanguageModel experiment path (setExpModelOrWait), the only code that programmatically overrode the user's picked model with an experiment-assigned one — the mechanism behind the intermittent reset to GPT 4.1/Sonnet 4.

rows.title: Copilot NEVER gets the line number correct
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and screenshot. This is being tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/280523, where the team confirmed that Copilot can read the correct file content and later report an incorrect line range; this report adds a macOS example with offsets ranging from roughly 10 to 400 lines.

/duplicate of #280523
rows.verifyEvidence: Both report that the chat model gives line numbers or ranges that don't match the file; the off-by-N locations come from the same model-side line attribution, so fixing B fixes A's ask. B is newer.

rows.title: Chat: Current file attachment gets stuck after closing file
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for reporting this, João. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/addd8a9e3c17917cb9aa7dc08cfcd7f9ed009a3f and shipped in 1.110 — the implicit context now clears when all editors are closed. Please reopen if you still see this on a current build.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff clears implicit context when no active editor exists, fixing the stale-value guard (newValue undefined + hasValue true) that kept the closed file's selection attached with no way to remove it.

rows.title: Vscode goes blank, loses all windows and activity bar & explorer.

Thanks for the report. It's been a while since the screen recording was requested — could you still reproduce this on a recent VS Code build (1.102+)? A short gif (https://gifcap.dev is handy) showing the blank activity bar would help us investigate. Without a visual reproduction, we're unable to narrow this down.

As a reminder, `info-needed` issues are automatically closed after 7 days without a reply.

rows.title: Deprecated link for Azure Models
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional context. The current Azure OpenAI REST documentation still specifies `https://{resource}.openai.azure.com` for inference endpoints: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/reference. VS Code also preserves fully resolved custom endpoint URLs, so replacing the documented hostname with `*.cognitiveservices.azure.com` would not be correct. Closing this as the current behavior is intentional.

rows.title: Image attachments aren't serialized properly
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for filing this. The serialization of image attachments was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/8c3bcf84aa3 ("fix image carousel attachments + persistent images + serialize them better"), which is on `main` and should ship in the next stable release. Images should now persist properly across reloads. Please reopen if you still see this on a recent Insiders build.
rows.verifyEvidence: Draft attachments now persist via marshalling stringify/parse ($base64) in a separate memento instead of JSON.stringify, which mangled image Uint8Array payloads — exactly the reload-then-hover breakage the report describes.

rows.title: Git - Lack of seamless navigation between files in Diff View for code review
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the request. Next/previous changed-file navigation from the SCM diff view is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/24389. This report adds the VS Code 1.105.1/macOS context and the request to move between files without selecting each entry in Source Control.

/duplicate of #24389
rows.verifyEvidence: Both ask for the same capability: moving to the next or previous changed file from the diff view without clicking it in the Source Control list. B's title and its 'navigate through changed files' bullet cover this.

rows.title: Electron wants to find devices on the local network
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report — this was a confusing prompt for sure. The root cause was a missing `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` in the app's Info.plist: without it, macOS fell back to showing the raw framework name "Electron" instead of a meaningful message.

This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/eb756b17065a333741c5c1a88d25cf57b3ee4cd9 and shipped in VS Code 1.116.0. The prompt now shows a proper usage description explaining that the app uses the local network for DNS resolution and connecting to local services.

If you're still seeing the old prompt on a current build, please open a new issue.
rows.verifyEvidence: The report is an unexplained macOS local-network prompt on launch; the diff inserts NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription into the signed app's (and embedded app's) Info.plist, supplying the DNS-resolution rationale the prompt lacked.

rows.title: Chat close button disappears in narrowest width

The fix shipped in 1.131.0.

rows.title: Expand Thinking section pushes chat layout upwards
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/489f3ab874ffa3290bb56f52c5ae75c6883daea2 via https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/325198. rows.title: Timeline does not track renames

Thanks for the report and detailed reproduction. /duplicate of #205244
rows.verifyEvidence: Same root cause: the git timeline uses --follow but opens pre-rename entries under the current filename. A gets 'file not found' and B gets a blank diff, because the old path is never tracked (e.g. via --name-status).

Since February 2026, the Copilot extension acquires a power save blocker during active chat/agent requests, which prevents the system from going to sleep while the agent is processing. The blocker is automatically released shortly after the request completes. This was shipped in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/de441dc178462184fb8772bfff47d325f752bf3e. - **Are you behind a proxy, firewall, or VPN?** If so, have you configured `http.proxy` in VS Code settings?

Please note that issues labeled `info-needed` will be auto-closed after **7 days** without a reply.

rows.title: provideLanguageModelChatResponse CancellationToken not work

The fix is on `main` and should ship in the next stable release. Please reopen or file a new issue if you still see this on an Insiders build.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff wraps the provider token in a local CancellationTokenSource kept in a pending map and adds a $cancelLanguageModelChatRequest RPC that cancels it, so provideLanguageModelChatResponse's token now fires on stop.

rows.title: Grok Stuck in repetition

If we don't hear back within 7 days this will be auto-closed, but please feel free to reopen if you can still reproduce it.

rows.title: 3 Days of Messages Disappeared from Chat
O novo modelo Gemini 3 Pro está MUITO LENTO
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. To understand whether this is something VS Code can address (vs. inherent model inference latency on Gemini's side), could you please:

1. Confirm this still happens on the **latest stable** VS Code build.
2. Clarify whether the same prompts are faster when using the Gemini API directly (e.g. via AI Studio) — this helps distinguish a VS Code overhead issue from model-side latency.
3. If possible, capture a **performance profile** (Help > Open Process Explorer, or Developer Tools > Performance tab) during the slow thinking phase.

Without this information it's hard to tell if VS Code is introducing overhead or if the model's thinking time is expected. Note: issues labeled `info-needed` are auto-closed after 7 days without a reply. Thanks!

rows.title: Markdown code segments in chat disappear after editing last prompt.

rows.title: Chat Interface Stealing Focus / Opening By Default
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. The behavior you're describing — the secondary sidebar (with Chat) opening automatically when you open a workspace for the first time — is controlled by the `workbench.secondarySideBar.defaultVisibility` setting, which defaults to `visibleInWorkspace`.

To prevent this, set it to `hidden` in your user settings:

```json
"workbench.secondarySideBar.defaultVisibility": "hidden"
```

This was introduced in VS Code 1.104 — see the [release notes](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_104#_chat-view-default-visibility). Once set at the user level, it applies globally across all workspaces. After a workspace has been opened once, VS Code restores the last layout state for that workspace on subsequent opens.

Closing as the existing setting covers this scenario. Please reopen if the setting doesn't resolve your use case.

Thanks for the suggestion and for thinking about VS Code's future on mobile platforms.

Migrating VS Code from Electron to Tauri would be a fundamental architectural rewrite of the entire platform layer — this isn't something the project plans to undertake. Electron is deeply integrated into how VS Code works (process model, native APIs, windowing, IPC), and replacing it is far beyond a migration.

For using VS Code on tablets (Android or iPad), you can use [vscode.dev](https://vscode.dev) today — it runs in any modern browser and gives you the core editing experience without needing a native install.

rows.title: Visual Studio Code Lagging Despite Adequate System Resources (HP Laptop, Intel Core i7 8th Gen, 16GB RAM)
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. Looking at your system info, the key issue jumps out: **your VS Code is running entirely on software rendering (SwiftShader)** — all GPU acceleration is disabled. This means every frame is being painted by the CPU instead of the GPU, which will cause exactly the lag you're describing regardless of available RAM.

Could you please try the following and report back?

1. **Update your Intel GPU drivers** — your Intel UHD 620 drivers may be outdated or misconfigured. Download the latest from [Intel's support site](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download-center/home.html).
2. **Check for forced software rendering** — run `code --status` and look for GPU-related flags. Also check if any group policy or antivirus is blocking GPU access.
3. **Test with extensions disabled** — run `code --disable-extensions` to rule out extension overhead (you have 43 extensions installed).
4. **Capture a performance trace** — Help > Open Process Explorer to see which processes consume CPU, and use `F1 > Developer: Startup Performance` to share timing data.

Please share the results so we can narrow this down. Note: issues labeled `info-needed` will auto-close after 7 days without a reply.

High CPU after update: cpptools repeatedly retries LanguageModelProxy model resolution in Remote-WSL extension host
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and logs — this was very helpful in diagnosing the feedback loop.

The root cause was that VS Code's `onDidChangeLanguageModels` event fired on every model metadata update (not just when models were added/removed), which caused extensions listening to the event and calling `selectChatModels` to spin in an unbounded CPU-pinning loop. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ca62bf6f0b52fe665c212535b6458098e93bbb33 and shipped in VS Code 1.123.0 — the event now only fires when the set of model identifiers actually changes.

Please update to 1.123.0 or later and confirm the issue is resolved. If you still see elevated CPU from model resolution, please open a new issue with fresh logs.
rows.verifyEvidence: Diff removes the recursive re-resolve loop in selectLanguageModels/getLanguageModelByIdentifier and suppresses metadata-only onChatModelsChange churn — exactly the CPU-pinning retry feedback loop emitting the reported 'Could not find model ... resolve again' spam.

2. Report it through the [GitHub Copilot community discussions](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/categories/copilot) so the content-safety team can investigate Korean-language filtering.

rows.title: Feature Request: "Send to AI Chat" from Markdown/Text Editor Use Case
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the suggestion! The functionality you're describing is actually already built into VS Code:

- **Add File to Chat** — right-click a file tab or use the editor context menu → "Add File to Chat", or run the command from the Command Palette (`workbench.action.chat.attachFile`). This attaches the entire file as context to the Chat view.
- **Add Selection to Chat** — select text in the editor, right-click → "Add Selection to Chat" (`workbench.action.chat.attachSelection`). This attaches just the selected portion.
- **Add Context…** — the `+` button / paperclip in the Chat input lets you pick files, folders, or selections to attach.
- **`#file` references** — type `#file:` in the Chat input to reference any file inline.

These work with any file type, including `.md` files, and attach the content as context for the AI conversation. Since this is already available, I'm closing this as already covered by the current design. If there's a specific gap these don't address, please feel free to open a new issue with details!

rows.title: TUI `Shift+Enter` causes SEND request instead of newline
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. This is working as designed — VS Code's terminal now supports the [kitty keyboard protocol](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/) (enabled by default via `terminal.integrated.enableKittyKeyboardProtocol`), which lets programs in the terminal distinguish modifier+key combinations like Shift+Enter from plain Enter. It's the `codex` TUI that's choosing to interpret Shift+Enter as "send" rather than "newline".

As a workaround, you can disable the protocol in your settings:
```json
"terminal.integrated.enableKittyKeyboardProtocol": false
```

Alternatively, the codex CLI itself could handle this differently — I see you've already filed https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16445 which is the right place for that request.

Alacritty and iTerm2 also support this protocol, so the behavior difference you see may be because codex doesn't request the enhanced mode in those terminals (or they handle negotiation differently).

Copilot Request id: fb659a80-8063-4528-acf7-d39a9e3a0bad  GH Request Id: 2E88:35A2AE:847C5B:9214A7:69D697A5  Reason: Request Failed: 400 {"message":"messages.1.content.14.image.source.base64.data: At least one of the image dimensions exceed max allowed size for many-image requests: 2000 pixels"}

rows.title: Copilot Chat fails on macOS arm64 with Electron fetcher: “Cannot convert argument to a ByteString … char 65279 (U+FEFF)” (regression between 1.110.1 and 1.115.0)
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and diagnostics. This was tracked down to a UTF-8 BOM character (U+FEFF) ending up in the `telemetry.devDeviceId` value, which is then sent as an HTTP header in Copilot API requests. Since the BOM character exceeds the ByteString limit of 255, undici rejects every request.

This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/15c518a9b04bd5e376279cd3daa6127fed9a3dc0 and shipped in VS Code **1.121.0**. Updating to 1.121.0 or later should resolve the issue. If you still see this on a current build, please open a new issue.
rows.verifyEvidence: Diff strips a leading U+FEFF BOM from the device id returned by @vscode/deviceid, the value propagated into request headers — exactly the index-0 char 65279 header that broke Electron/undici ByteString conversion.

rows.title: Copilot Chat: skills should declare capability requirements, and the platform should surface unmet ones
C/C++ macros screw with bracket colouring
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. This is a known limitation of bracket pair colorization — the algorithm works on the flat token stream and doesn't understand C/C++ preprocessor conditionals like `#ifdef`/`#else`. When brackets are split across preprocessor branches, the colorizer sees mismatched pairs.

This has been reported and discussed several times (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/222923, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/175839, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/212860, among others) and the conclusion has been that this is as-designed: fixing it would require either the TextMate grammar to suppress one branch or a fundamentally different bracket-matching architecture, neither of which is currently planned.

Your suggestion about treating `#if`/`#else` paths as separate branches is thoughtful, but it would require significant changes to the bracket pair colorizer's model. Closing as as-designed, consistent with the prior decisions.

rows.title: RunInTerminalTool hangs forever when trackIdleOnPrompt is stuck in Executing state
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the thorough write-up and eval evidence, Megan. The hang described here — state machine stuck in Executing with both schedulers cancelled — has been addressed through multiple commits on main:

- **64e09196a3e** (PR #312387): initial fallback scheduler for the no-data-at-all case
- **8894b02366e** (PR #312854): rich-to-basic downgrade when SI breaks mid-command
- **ade6340a22b** (PR #313312): `executingFallbackScheduler` — a 30s data-idle fallback that fires in the Executing state, directly addressing the dead state described here

The current `trackIdleOnPrompt` on main now reschedules `executingFallbackScheduler` on every data event in Executing state and fires it after 30s of silence, plus has a 5-minute hard-cap safety net. These shipped in 1.118.0. Closing as fixed — please reopen if you still see hangs on the latest build.
rows.verifyEvidence: The added 60s hard cap only fires when state is Initial or Prompt; the reported hang occurs after C/D advances state to Executing, which the new guard explicitly excludes, so the described dead state persists.

rows.title: Explorer File Tree Sort Order Bug
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report. The Explorer's default sort order intentionally uses **natural sorting** — numeric substrings within filenames are compared as numbers, not character-by-character. That's why `Z10X` (numeric part `10`) sorts before `Z106` (numeric part `106`): `10 < 106`.

If you'd prefer pure ASCII/Unicode character ordering (matching `ls` behavior), you can set:

```json
"explorer.sortOrderLexicographicOptions": "unicode"
```

This will sort names by raw Unicode code points, giving you the order you expect. Closing this as the current behavior is by design, with an existing setting to get the alternative ordering.

Memory Leak in Screenshot Annotation Tool
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. Looking at the code, `startTextEdit` in `screenshotAnnotation.ts` does use raw `addEventListener` instead of `addDisposableListener` on the textarea — that's a code-hygiene issue worth tidying. However, each time a new text edit starts, `commitTextEdit()` is called first, which runs `cleanupTextEditor()` and removes the previous textarea from the DOM. Since no other reference keeps the old element alive, its listeners become eligible for garbage collection. So the "exponential growth" described in the report shouldn't occur in practice.

Could you share a heap snapshot or performance recording showing actual memory accumulation? Without concrete evidence of a leak, it's hard to treat this as more than a style cleanup. Note that `info-needed` issues auto-close after 7 days without a reply.
