rows.title: Accessibility: Webview body element has invalid role="document" (WCAG 4.1.2 violation)
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and the WCAG reference — accessibility reports are always appreciated.

However, the `role="document"` on the webview body is intentional and was added specifically to **fix** an accessibility problem (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/93435, fixing https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/93087). The reason: VS Code's root element carries `role="application"`, which causes all nested content — including webview iframes — to inherit application semantics. Without the explicit `role="document"` override, screen readers would treat webview content as application UI instead of browsable document content, breaking browse-mode navigation.

This was reviewed and approved by an accessibility expert (Marco Zehe) in the PR discussion. While `<body>` does have an implicit `document` role in a standalone page, that implicit role is overridden by the inherited `application` context — so the explicit `role="document"` is necessary here.

Removing it would actually regress accessibility for screen reader users. Closing as by-design.

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. The integrated terminal requires Windows build 18309 or later for conpty support, and your system is on build 14393 (Windows Server 2016 / Windows 10 1607). Since winpty was removed in VS Code 1.109 (see [the release notes](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_109#_removal-of-winpty-support)), the terminal cannot launch on Windows versions below build 18309.

Your options are:
- **Upgrade Windows** to a version with conpty support (build 18309+, i.e. Windows 10 version 1903 or later)
- **Use VS Code 1.108 or earlier**, which still included winpty as a fallback

Closing this as the current behavior is by design.

rows.title: Mouse drag selection stops working in Monaco editor after resuming from sleep
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and the thorough troubleshooting steps — the graphics driver reset clue is especially helpful.

Looking at your system info, your GPU is running on **Microsoft Basic Render Driver** (a Windows software fallback) with all GPU acceleration disabled. This is unusual for desktop use and suggests either no dedicated GPU driver is installed, or it failed to load.

The fact that Win+Ctrl+Shift+B (graphics driver reset) temporarily restores drag selection strongly points to a graphics subsystem / Chromium compositor issue rather than a VS Code editor bug.

Could you help us narrow this down?

1. **Do you have a dedicated GPU** (AMD/NVIDIA/Intel)? If so, is its driver installed and up to date?
2. Does the issue reproduce if you install the correct GPU driver so VS Code uses hardware acceleration instead of the Basic Render Driver?
3. Does this reproduce in a Chromium-based browser (e.g. Chrome/Edge) with a Monaco editor instance (like https://microsoft.github.io/monaco-editor/) after sleep?

This will help us determine whether the fix belongs in VS Code, in Electron/Chromium, or in the graphics driver. Note: issues marked `info-needed` are auto-closed after 7 days without a reply.

Agent Host BYOK doubles customendpoint URL path → 404
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and the time spent tracing the code.

I looked into the path you described, and I believe the root cause you identified may not be accurate for how the BYOK proxy actually routes requests on current `main`. Specifically:

- The Copilot SDK never receives the customendpoint URL from `chatLanguageModels.json` directly. Instead, `resolveByokSessionConfig` in `copilotSessionLauncher.ts` configures each BYOK provider with a `baseUrl` pointing at the **local loopback proxy** (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v/customendpoint`), not at `api.deepseek.com`.
- The SDK appends `/chat/completions` to this **proxy** URL, making `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v/customendpoint/chat/completions`.
- The proxy extracts the vendor, then forwards the request to the renderer's LM API via IPC — which calls `ILanguageModelsService.sendChatRequest()`, the same path Chat view uses.
- The renderer's `customEndpointProvider` resolves the actual URL, and it already handles URLs that contain `/chat/completions` (via `hasExplicitApiPath`).

So the URL doubling you described shouldn't occur through this code path. The real failure is likely elsewhere. Could you help us narrow it down?

1. Enable trace-level logging (`Developer: Set Log Level…` → Trace) and share the full agent host logs when the error occurs.
2. Confirm that `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled` is set to `true` in your settings.
3. Are you on VS Code Insiders? If so, please update to the latest Insiders build and retry.

This issue will auto-close after 7 days without a reply, so please follow up when you can. Thanks!

rows.title: Copilot Chat can invoke an MCP tool before its adapter is registered (undefined.invoke)
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and the linked repro in https://github.com/MarkBovee/nebu-ctx/issues/29 — this is a real timing bug rather than something in your MCP server.

Tracing it in `LanguageModelToolsService#invokeTool` (src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/languageModelToolsService.ts): the tool's `impl` is checked once early on, but several `await`s happen before it's actually invoked (hook resolution, `prepareToolInvocation`, confirmation). If `McpLanguageModelToolContribution`'s tool-sync logic disposes and re-registers that same tool in the meantime (e.g. right after the server's `tools/list` settles), the disposer clears `impl` on the stale entry your call is still holding, and the eventual `tool.impl.invoke(...)` call throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'invoke')`.

The fix likely needs to re-resolve the tool/impl from the registry immediately before invoking, rather than trusting the reference captured earlier in the function. Routing to the MCP/chat tools area for a maintainer to pick up.

rows.labels: bug, info-needed, linux, regression, network, agent-host
rows.proposedComment: Thanks everyone for the detailed follow-up, especially for capturing the crash dumps and running the isolated `dlopen` tests. As confirmed in the investigation, the segfault happens inside the dynamic linker (`ld-linux`) during lazy relocation of the system `libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0`, reproducible even outside of VS Code entirely — so this isn't a VS Code code defect. As a workaround, try running with `LD_BIND_NOW=1` set. I'd recommend following up with the CachyOS/Arch package maintainers, since a newer glibc or webkit2gtk build may already address this. Closing as not reproducible on our side, but feel free to reopen with distro-side findings if useful.

rows.title: Built-in skills are not returned by the sessionless commands.list API (skills unavailable in sessionless chat input completions)
Bug in Settings / workbench.colorCustomizations
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report — I was able to trace this to VS Code's own theme configuration schema, not an extension or theme issue. In src/vs/workbench/services/themes/common/themeConfiguration.ts, the theme-scoped `workbench.colorCustomizations` schema (`{ "[Theme Name]": { ... } }`) builds its object schema as `{ $ref: workbenchColorsSchemaId, additionalProperties: false }`. Per JSON Schema semantics (and how `vscode-json-languageservice` resolves schemas), keywords placed as siblings of `$ref` are ignored unless wrapped in `allOf` — so the referenced color properties never actually get merged in for the theme-scoped case, `additionalProperties: false` then rejects every key, and there's nothing to drive autocomplete. The top-level (non-scoped) schema doesn't have this problem because it already uses `allOf: [{ $ref: workbenchColorsSchemaId }]` with no sibling keywords — which is exactly the pattern that works in your example #1. The fix should be to apply the same `allOf` wrapping to the theme-scoped `workbenchColors` schema object. Routing to the theming/settings-schema area for a fix.

rows.title: Memory leak: main process buffers terminal output indefinitely in an unbounded Event.buffer (1.15M events / 602 MB) -> OOM closes all windows
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the extremely well-documented report — the heap snapshot, retainer chain, and crash dumps make this easy to follow. Tracing it in the current source: `Event.buffer` (src/vs/base/common/event.ts) never caps its internal array and only stops buffering once a first listener has *ever* attached for the life of the buffered event; `ProxyChannel.fromService` (src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts) shares that single buffered event across the whole IPC channel's lifetime. If a pty host process becomes fully orphaned (matching the 'Process had no disconnect runners but was an orphan' log line, which already exists in src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts) and no window ever (re)connects to it, its output event buffer has no listener to trigger a flush and grows without bound until OOM. This lines up with the second reporter's crash dumps showing the pty host process as the one that actually died. Routing to the terminal area for a fix — likely either bounding/disposing the IPC event buffer, or reaping orphaned pty host processes sooner so they stop producing before the buffer can grow unbounded.

rows.title: Codespaces: ToDoWrite issues in .agent.md file
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed write-up. A few things are getting conflated here that are worth separating: `todo` is the only supported frontmatter identifier for the native Todo tool (with `todos` as a legacy alias) — `TodoWrite` and `manage_todo_list` are internal identifiers used by other agent harnesses (Claude Code, Copilot CLI) and aren't meant to be valid `.agent.md` tool references. Body-text mentions of a tool name are natural-language hints to the model, not deterministic activations, so they won't reliably trigger the tool the way `tools: [todo]` does. There is an existing 'unknown tool reference' diagnostic in the prompt validator that should flag unsupported names in frontmatter — if that isn't showing up for you in Codespaces Stable, that'd be useful to confirm separately. Routing this to the chat team so they can consider clearer documentation/validation messaging around tool-name aliasing across surfaces.

rows.title: [regression] GitHub Copilot chat up arrow deletes current chat content.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed writeup. This traces back to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328269, which intentionally removed the `!isComposing` clause from the built-in `history.showPrevious`/`history.showNext` keybindings — it had become dead code once composing keystrokes are normalized to `KEY_IN_COMPOSITION` earlier in the pipeline. Keybinding overrides need to match the built-in `when` clause exactly to suppress it, so your existing override (which still includes `!isComposing`) no longer disables the command. You've already found the right answer: drop `!isComposing` from your override so it reads `historyNavigationBackwardsEnabled && historyNavigationWidgetFocus && !suggestWidgetVisible` (and the same for `showNext`). I'll close this as a question since it's not a product defect, but flagging it here so the discussion is documented for anyone else hitting the same stale-override issue.

Modern UI's editor tabs are intentionally re-themed with their own color tokens rather than reusing the classic `tab.*` keys for active/hover fills: `modernTab.activeBackground`, `modernTab.hoverBackground`, `modernTab.activeForeground`, and `modernTab.hoverForeground` (set these via `workbench.colorCustomizations`). rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and screenshots. This isn't a settings bug in the traditional sense — `workbench.experimental.modernUI` ships with `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`, so VS Code fetches an A/B treatment for it (via the experimentation/assignment service) and applies it as a *default* value once extensions and assignments are resolved, which explains why it only shows up after a restart and only for some users. It doesn't write anything into your settings.json — you can override it back explicitly by adding `"workbench.experimental.modernUI": false` to your user settings, which takes precedence over the experiment-provided default. That said, the lack of any visible notice when an experiment changes core visual appearance is a fair concern worth keeping open for the team to consider (e.g. a one-time notification when this kind of experiment flips a visual default).

rows.title: Run and Debug Breakpoints Section disappears
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the clear repro steps. I traced this in the current source: the Breakpoints view is shown only when at least one breakpoint exists, or the 'simple' debug UX has switched to 'default' (a launch configuration + enabled debugger, or an active session), or a debug session has actually been started (`CONTEXT_HAS_DEBUGGED`). If you only set/remove a breakpoint without a launch configuration or a started session, none of those hold, so the panel — and its Run and Debug view-picker entry — intentionally hides again. This matches the 'simple' debug UX designed to declutter the Run and Debug view for users without a configured debugger, so I'm marking this as-designed rather than a bug. If you'd like the panel to stay visible once shown in a session, that'd be a good feature request.

rows.title: [BUG] Custom Endpoint context window size is bloated by +16K in UI & context manager, causing potential backend context overflow
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report and math. I traced this to `resolveModelTokenLimits` in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/byok/common/byokProvider.ts`: when a Custom Endpoint config sets `maxInputTokens` (e.g. `212000`) without also setting `contextWindow`, the total window is intentionally derived as `maxInputTokens + maxOutputTokens` for backward compatibility — that's the exact +16384 you're seeing (your configured `maxOutputTokens`). This is documented in the settings schema and covered by a dedicated unit test.

To match your server's real `-c 212000` total, set `contextWindow: 212000` instead of (or in addition to) `maxInputTokens` — when `contextWindow` is present it becomes the source of truth, and `maxInputTokens` is derived as `contextWindow - maxOutputTokens`. The resolver also clamps `maxOutputTokens`/`maxInputTokens` so input+output can never exceed the resolved window, so there's no overflow risk from VS Code's side once `contextWindow` is set correctly. Closing as as-designed, but happy to revisit if this doesn't resolve the discrepancy for you.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed repro. I checked this against the actual Markdown parser VS Code's chat view uses (`marked.js`), and `__init__` on its own line legitimately satisfies CommonMark's emphasis rules — there's no alphanumeric character right before the opening `__` or right after the closing `__`, so both delimiters are valid emphasis markers and it renders as bold. This matches the CommonMark spec, not a rendering bug.

As your own tests show, wrapping identifiers in backticks (`` `__init__` ``) renders them correctly as literal text — that's the expected way to reference code symbols in Markdown, and it's on the model to use that formatting for identifiers rather than emitting them as bare text. Closing as as-designed, but happy to revisit if there's a case where even fenced/inline code renders incorrectly.

rows.title: Remote SSH: Copilot incorrectly requests external-file permission for workspace paths involving symlinks
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and repro steps. I traced this in the source: `getWorkspaceFileExternalConfirmation` in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/toolUtils.ts` fully resolves the requested file's real path (via `resolveRealPathForNonexistent`, which calls `realpath()` unconditionally when the file exists) but then checks containment against the *unresolved* workspace-folder URI from `WorkingDirectory`/`IWorkspaceService`. When the workspace root itself is opened through a symlink or bind mount (common on Remote SSH), the resolved file path can never match the workspace folder's original path, so every in-workspace file is flagged as external. The existing tests in `toolUtils.spec.ts` happen to realpath the workspace directory before use, which is why this gap wasn't caught. The fix likely needs to resolve the workspace folder's own real path once and compare against that, rather than the raw workspace folder URI.

rows.title: Github Copilot Tool-result truncation splits UTF-16 surrogate pairs → HTTP 400 `invalid_request_body` on OpenAI-family models (Claude models unaffected)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the very thorough report and transcript analysis — this pinpointed a real bug. Since 0.63.0, request bodies now go through `stringifyJsonBody()` (extensions/copilot/src/platform/networking/common/jsonBody.ts), which detects and repairs unpaired UTF-16 surrogates before any JSON body is sent, regardless of which tool introduced them or which model family the request targets. There's even a unit test (`jsonBody.spec.ts`) covering exactly the "tool result truncated mid-emoji" scenario you described. That should prevent the `invalid_request_body` 400 you were hitting. The separate, more cosmetic gap — that `grep_search`'s line truncation isn't surrogate-boundary-aware the way file reads already are — would be a good small follow-up if you'd like to file it, but it's no longer what causes the failure. Please reopen or file a new issue if you still see the 400 on the latest Copilot Chat build. The fix is on main and not yet in a stable release — you can verify on Insiders.

rows.title: [AutomaticInstructionsCollector] Core vs extension instructions mismatch filling the chat log
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report, and thanks @aeschli for the lead. Traced it: `AgentInstructionsLocator.listNestedAgentMDs` (extensions/copilot/src/platform/promptFiles/vscode-node/agentInstructionsLocator.ts) calls `vscode.workspace.findFiles('**/AGENTS.md', undefined, ...)`, and per the API docs that only applies `files.exclude`, not `search.exclude` — which is where the default `node_modules`/`bower_components` exclusion lives. Core's own AGENTS.md search (`PromptFilesLocator.findAgentMDsInFolder`) merges both via `getExcludes()`, so it correctly skips node_modules while the extension's parity-check reimplementation doesn't. The fix is to route this through the existing `ISearchService.findFilesWithDefaultExcludes` helper already used elsewhere in the extension, which applies the same combined excludes as core.

Markdown syntax highlighter: mismatched brackets in code blocks in hyperlinks
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report — this traces to a real gap in the markdown grammar contribution. extensions/markdown-basics/package.json doesn't declare a `tokenTypes` mapping for the inline code-span scope (`markup.inline.raw.string.markdown`), unlike css/html/js/typescript-basics, so VS Code's bracket matcher never classifies brackets inside backtick-quoted text as being inside a "string" and doesn't skip them. That's why the opening `[` of the link gets matched to the `]` inside the code span instead of the link's real closing bracket. Keeping this open as a bug for the markdown grammar.

cursor up/down is confused by selection
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report. As Alex noted, this behavior is intentional — when a selection exists, down/right collapse to the end of the selection, and up/left collapse to the beginning. This is consistent with SublimeText and other editors, and the logic is explicit in our cursor movement code.

The request for an option to change this hasn't gained community traction over the years, so I'm closing this as designed. If there's renewed interest, feel free to open a new issue and we can revisit.

rows.title: Handle pasting code from column selection specially
Input variables only work with one configuration in a compound launch config
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The compound-launch failure caused by concurrent input prompts was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0f2239fc7c2703312928b6f7ff9ce6642d2e3354 and completed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0dddb856fd89d55b1dadc97ab49aca800f3eb8ff; the same symptom was verified resolved in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/141514 and the fix shipped in VS Code 1.71.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: Compound configs resolve concurrently, so their input-variable prompts race and only one session survives; the commit serializes every user-input-requiring resolution step through a Queue, exactly the reported mechanism.

rows.title: [json] jsonValidation fileMatch is confusing when used with URIs
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and discussion. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-json-languageservice/commit/c0d22f67f57d09f40c7d60ae9f39c3da5ad7e436 changed schema association matching to ignore URI queries and fragments, and current VS Code uses that behavior. A jsonValidation.fileMatch pattern matching the document's scheme and path therefore no longer needs to account for those suffixes; the reported validation failure is resolved.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff adds normalizeResourceForMatching, which strips the query and fragment from the resource URI before fileMatch is tested. That is the reported mechanism: a `custom:/…something.todo?foo` URI now matches `*.todo`. The new tests cover query and fragment positives.

rows.title: Auto closing brackets should try to balance brackets
[html] bracket matching in strings
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and detailed reproduction. This behavior was resolved by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ff757ef8f467015a91b0f8052e7ef3b611bc538e, which removed `<` and `>` from HTML's editor bracket pairs; comparison operators inside quoted attributes therefore no longer corrupt bracket matching or bracket-based smart selection. The fix shipped in 1.77.0.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff removes the ["<", ">"] pair from HTML's bracket config, so a `<` inside an attribute string like `something <= 0` can no longer be taken as an opening bracket and mismatched. That is the reported defect.

rows.title: Expose vscode remote reconnecting UI.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. Extensions should not be able to block the entire workbench while reconnecting; current Remote reconnection feedback is intentionally presented as a non-blocking status indicator. Extensions can surface equivalent connection progress with `window.withProgress` using `ProgressLocation.Window` or `ProgressLocation.Notification`, so closing this as designed.

rows.title: Add a shortcut or a button to restart extension host.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d7890fa51fdd3cafa06325c9739608a29cba677c and shipped in VS Code 1.42. Use **Developer: Restart Extension Host** from the Command Palette; you can also assign that command a keyboard shortcut.
rows.verifyEvidence: The commit registers a workbench action 'Developer: Restart Extension Host' (workbench.action.restartExtensionHost) calling extensionService.restartExtensionHost, delivering the requested command-palette/keybindable way to restart the extension host without restarting the editor.

rows.title: Terminal doesn't flush all line data before firing onExit
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the thorough report and repro. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/c2e9b6a63c01473c0b972448eb983194961cdbb1 and shipped in VS Code 1.48.0 — xterm data is now ensured to be parsed before exit fires. Both the team and the original reporter verified the fix at the time.

The later regression noted in the comments was tracked separately as https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/105159. If you're still seeing issues on a recent build, please open a new issue with updated reproduction steps.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff makes _onProcessExit await xterm write-parse completion before firing onExit, closing the race where a pseudoterminal task's final output was emitted after exit and thus never reached problem matchers.

rows.title: Terminal canvas context loss is not handled
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. This is now fully addressed on current VS Code:

- The canvas renderer was removed entirely from the terminal (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6cdd364d9336216c2a9c8d98a35d30275aa0a87d).
- WebGL context loss is handled gracefully — when the GPU reclaims the context, VS Code disposes the WebGL renderer and falls back to the DOM renderer.
- The upstream xterm.js issue (https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/2816) is also closed.

Closing as resolved. If you still see rendering issues after context loss on a recent build, please open a new issue with steps to reproduce.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff deletes the xterm canvas addon, its enable/dispose paths, and the 'canvas' gpuAcceleration option entirely, so the terminal no longer creates a 2d canvas context that can be lost — the reported unhandled path cannot occur.

rows.title: Can't click to set/clear breakpoint when a gutter decoration exists
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and follow-up context. The remaining inability to set a breakpoint over another glyph decoration is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/179725, which tracks the dedicated breakpoint lane needed for this scenario; https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/185814 is a related implementation task.

/duplicate of #179725
rows.verifyEvidence: B's planned glyph-margin rework gives breakpoints their own lane, apart from other decorations. That fixes A's case, where a Bookmarks gutter decoration blocks clicking to set or clear a breakpoint.
